# Native file resource qualification

The Unix adapter selects approved directory roots once and retains their descriptors. Source paths walk single components without following links, verify each opened identity and recheck the complete parent chain. Relative lookup retains declaring-directory, project and explicit-data-root order; only a genuinely absent entry permits fallback. Permission and file-kind failures stop before later candidates. The existing approved-root policy remains in force pending the separate #1751 approval.

A first capture checks metadata size before allocation, reads in 64 KiB chunks through at most one byte beyond the trusted ceiling, compares a fresh bounded read directly, and retains immutable bytes. Repeated paths and physical hard-link aliases share a snapshot; each accepted alias is verified directly on reuse. Changed or over-limit replies add neither a snapshot nor an alias. The policy bounds 64 selected roots, 65,536 UTF-8 bytes per authored path, 1,024 snapshots/path keys and 67,108,864 retained content bytes. These capacities do not bound total process memory.

Eleven native tests cover exact byte ceilings, cached growth/shrink, empty captures, root/fallback order, links and escaped paths, accepted aliases, replaced root spellings, normalized approved-root aliases, and terminal permission failures. The permission regressions fail against the initial candidate before the correction.

The private R bridge supplies raw UTF-8 paths, raw bytes and capture counters through registered handles. It performs no YAML interpretation, source typing or table inference. Installed R qualification replays all seventeen unchanged original corpus reports twice with real file inspection/capture, the seven independently authored zero-read metadata failures, the unchanged complete Parquet success and nineteen Parquet failures, exact CSV publication, and cached save gates. Python is absent from PATH throughout. Byte-policy checks also cover copied R buffers, wrong arguments, changed contents, symbolic links, approved-root escapes and serialized expired handles.

This qualifies a Unix study-source adapter. Entry/layer/environment/codelist capture, public file APIs, production atomic publication, Windows native file transport and callback retirement remain separate work. Existing truth and reference-assisted inventory levels do not change.
